task: bid on an eBay auction as a buyer: find an auction listing, review item condition, seller rating, and shipping, place a bid by setting a maximum bid, confirm the bid, and see the resulting bid status; complete when the bid-confirmed state ("You're the highest bidder" or "You've been outbid") is on screen. Surface pinned: the eBay website or app. Variants: selling or listing items, dropshipping/reselling content, "Buy It Now" only purchases (that is ordinary shopping), and sniping-tool promotions do not belong.

tree.label: Win an eBay auction
tree.note: 1 where the account demands it - most keepers arrive signed in. 2 unless the listing is already at hand - ten keepers open on the target. then 3, then 4; T5mb runs 3.5 before anything else. 5 stages the bid - 5.2 replaces the bid box for the three accounts with no payment on file, and none of them ever bids. 6 owns the clock: snipers hold inside it, immediate bidders fall straight through to 6.6 (08WT, s_CE, B7Zu, fAtx). 7 whenever the outbid notice lands - it can interrupt 6 or follow it. 8 when the clock resolves; a loss ends there. 9 after a win, and 9.4 loops the whole task back to 2 - six times in Zkom. fx1m runs 5 and 6 across four windows at once.

children.label: Get into eBay
children.note: only two keepers touch 1.1 to 1.3 - one demos registration without submitting (s_CE), one signs in for real (08WT). the rest arrive signed in, and several run 1.4 as their first act.

questions.question: What eBay Bucks balance does the My eBay page show?
questions.why: The screen displays your current eBay Bucks balance and recent sales history, which could inform your bidding budget.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to check their available eBay Bucks or recent sales activity before starting a new search.
questions.check: What eBay Bucks balance does the My eBay page show?
questions.say_example: eBay Bucks balance <$4.12> - not touched

questions.question: Which regional eBay site should you go to, to start finding an auction?
questions.why: The browser is currently on a search engine, so you must explicitly enter the correct regional eBay domain to find relevant local listings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify their preferred regional marketplace, which directly impacts shipping costs and item availability.
questions.check: Which eBay regional domains do the search results show?
questions.say_example: The search shows more than one eBay site. I'll use ebay.com, the US one, so prices come in dollars.

questions.question: Is this the new-account registration form rather than the sign-in page?
questions.why: The screen displays a blank registration form requesting extensive personal details like your address and date of birth, which is unnecessary if you already have an account.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses control over their personal data privacy if the agent unnecessarily creates a new account using their sensitive information.
questions.check: Does the page show a new-account registration form asking for address and date of birth?
questions.say_example: This is the new-account page. It wants your address and birth date. You already have an account, so I'm going to sign in instead.

questions.question: Does the eBay email show an 'Activate Now' button?
questions.why: The email from eBay displays an 'Activate Now' button that must be clicked to complete registration and enable bidding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the certainty that their account is fully activated and actually capable of placing bids.
questions.check: Does the eBay email show an 'Activate Now' button?
questions.say_example: Clicked Activate Now in the eBay email - account live

questions.question: Which account credentials should I use to sign in?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Sign in to your account' form that requires a User ID and password to authenticate the session before proceeding.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide which specific account and identity will be tied to the auction bid and its potential financial obligation.
questions.check: Does the page show the sign-in form, and which saved accounts does it offer?
questions.say_example: eBay wants a sign-in before any bidding. Which account should I use? You'll type the password yourself.

questions.question: Do you want to save your eBay credentials in the VeriSoft password manager?
questions.why: The VeriSoft Single Sign On dialog box appeared with a prompt asking to record your logon information for ebay.com.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether your sensitive eBay password is saved to this third-party credential manager.
questions.check: Does a dialog ask to save the eBay password?
questions.say_example: A box popped up asking to save your password. I'm saying no, so nothing gets stored.

questions.question: Does the header show your username, confirming the sign-in?
questions.why: Seeing your personalized greeting and username in the header confirms you are authenticated and able to place bids.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the reassurance of confirming firsthand that the agent is operating under your specific identity.
questions.check: Does the page header show the account greeting or username?
questions.say_example: The page doesn't show you signed in. I'm signing in again before we go further.

children.label: Find an auction
children.note: one of 2.1 to 2.4 raises candidates - or none: ten keepers open already on the target listing. 2.5 to 2.7 narrow as the strategy demands, then 2.8. 2.9 sends a dead pick back to 2.8.

questions.question: What search term is entered in the search bar?
questions.why: The screen displays an empty search bar on the My eBay Summary page, which requires specific terms to locate the auction listing you want.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify the exact item, brand, or model they are interested in bidding on.
questions.check: What term does the search bar contain?
questions.say_example: Got it. Searching eBay for <a men's automatic watch>, auctions only.

questions.question: Did the search return zero exact matches and automatically show results for a different, autocorrected keyword?
questions.why: eBay will automatically swap your search term if it finds no exact matches, which can lead to browsing and bidding on items that are similar but not exactly what you specified.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to realize the agent is evaluating the wrong items because the platform silently altered the search query.
questions.check: Does the results page say it found no exact matches and is showing results for a different term?
questions.say_example: eBay found nothing for <your word>, so it's showing <another word> instead. These aren't exactly what you asked for.

questions.question: Is the Auction buying-format filter applied to the results?
questions.why: The search results currently display over 1,100 items with mixed buying formats, so selecting the 'Auction' filter ensures you only see listings you can actually bid on.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to browse 'Buy It Now' options that might offer a better or faster deal before committing to the auction format.
questions.check: Does the results page show the Auction filter as applied, and how many results remain?
questions.say_example: Found <1,100> listings, but most are Buy It Now. You want an auction, so I'm keeping auctions only. That leaves <214>.

questions.question: Are the top results marked Sponsored?
questions.why: The current search results are dominated by sponsored bulk lots with 'or Best Offer' pricing rather than the required auction format.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose control over refining the search criteria to ensure you are bidding on a single item rather than a wholesale lot.
questions.check: Which of the top results carry a Sponsored label?
questions.say_example: The first <two> results are ads, so I'm skipping those.

questions.question: What sort order is selected on the results page?
questions.why: The sort menu offers options like 'Best Match' and 'Ending Soonest', which determines whether you prioritize item relevance or finding auctions that are in their final seconds.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to decide whether to prioritize bidding on auctions ending immediately over waiting for better-matched items that close later.
questions.check: What sort order does the results page show as selected?
questions.say_example: The sort was Best Match, which is partly promoted. I'm sorting by ending soonest instead.

questions.question: Does the results page show the price filter applied?
questions.why: The screen shows the keypad with a partial entry and a 'Searching' state, meaning the results haven't actually loaded yet to confirm if the filter worked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately narrow down items within their budget if the agent misinterprets a loading screen as a failed filter.
questions.check: Does the results page show the price cap as applied, with results loaded?
questions.say_example: The price cap didn't take. I'm setting it again before we pick.

questions.question: Does the applied size filter match the size you asked for?
questions.why: The search results page showed over 1,100 results for the shoe, making it necessary to apply a size filter to find relevant listings.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify their exact shoe size to narrow down the search results.
questions.check: What size filter does the results page show as applied?
questions.say_example: The size filter is on <12>, but you asked for <5>. Fixing it.

questions.question: Do the results match the condition you asked for?
questions.why: The search results include a mix of brand new, certified refurbished, and pre-owned items, and applying a condition filter ensures you only spend time evaluating items that meet your quality standards.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to automatically weed out used or broken items that they have no intention of bidding on.
questions.check: What condition labels do the shown listings carry?
questions.say_example: You asked for new, but these mix in used ones. I'm filtering to new only.

questions.question: Which of the filtered auction items should you select to view?
questions.why: The search results display multiple options, such as an owl pendant ending in 29 seconds, and selecting one determines which specific auction you will evaluate.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to browse the other search results and choose the item that best fits your personal taste and budget.
questions.check: Which auction listings, prices and end times do the results show?
questions.say_example: Three fit. <The owl pendant>, <$4.20>, ends in <29 seconds>. <The silver chain>, <$6>, ends <tonight at 9>. <The bracelet>, <$5.50>, ends <tomorrow>. Which one?

questions.question: Are these the expected items from the seller you searched for?
questions.why: The screen displays 82 results for 'kiwanis_club_of_fort_frances', so you must confirm you are viewing the correct inventory before selecting an item.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally browse the seller's specific inventory and choose the exact item that interests you.
questions.check: Does the results header name the seller you asked for?
questions.say_example: These results are for <kiwanis_club_of_fort_frances>, but you asked for a different seller. I'm searching again.

questions.question: Does this listing actually allow you to place a bid?
questions.why: The screen showed 'Buy It Now' and 'Add to cart' options rather than a bid input, indicating this is a fixed-price item rather than an auction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks an unintended outright purchase or a stalled task if the agent cannot distinguish between fixed-price and auction listings.
questions.check: Does the page show a Place bid button, or only Buy It Now and Add to cart?
questions.say_example: This one is Buy It Now only. There's nothing to bid on, so I'm going back to the auctions.

children.label: Vet the listing
children.note: 3.1 in every keeper; 3.2 where the photos decide; 3.3 to 3.6 where the user bothers - the corpus mostly reads the panel and skips the rest, and C6qx reads the terms only after winning.

questions.question: Is there enough time on the countdown to check the seller and the description before bidding?
questions.why: The screen shows only 34 seconds remaining, forcing a trade-off between verifying the seller's reliability and successfully placing a bid in time.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their personal risk tolerance regarding unverified sellers when an auction is closing rapidly.
questions.check: How much time does the countdown show?
questions.say_example: Only <34> seconds left. That's not enough time to check the seller or the returns policy. Bid anyway, or let this one go?

questions.question: Does the listing say the seller accepts returns?
questions.why: The listing specifies a $5.50 shipping fee and a strict no-returns policy that you must accept if you win the auction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to weigh the total cost and the risk of the no-returns policy against your personal preferences before committing to buy.
questions.check: What does the listing's returns line say?
questions.say_example: This seller takes no returns. If you win it, it's yours, even if it's wrong.

questions.question: Does the listing state a shipping cost, or does it say 'Shipping not specified'?
questions.why: The screen indicated 'Shipping not specified' and a truncated description, which must be investigated to avoid unexpected costs or errors.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to avoid bidding on an item with unknown shipping costs or undisclosed defects.
questions.check: What does the listing's shipping line say?
questions.say_example: The listing doesn't say what shipping costs. It could be anything on top of the bid. Skip it, or ask the seller?

questions.question: Is the current bid displayed in your local currency, or does it include a foreign currency prefix like 'C $' or '£'?
questions.why: eBay mixes international listings into search results, and small visual currency prefixes drastically change the actual financial commitment due to exchange rates.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to accurately gauge the item's true cost if the agent reads the raw number but misses the visual currency indicator.
questions.check: What currency prefix does the price carry?
questions.say_example: Careful, that price is in Canadian dollars. <C $13.16> is about <$9.70> for you.

questions.question: What is the current bid and how much time remains on the auction?
questions.why: Monitoring the current bid of $33.00 and the countdown timer helps determine the optimal moment to place your maximum bid.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally time your bid at the last possible second to maximize your chances of winning at the lowest price.
questions.check: What current bid and time remaining does the listing show?
questions.say_example: Here's the one you picked. The bid is at <$33>, and it ends in <2 hours and 10 minutes>.

questions.question: Does the listing say it may not ship to your country?
questions.why: The screen displayed a warning that the item 'May not ship to Philippines', meaning you could win the auction but be unable to receive the item.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to avoid committing money to an auction that cannot actually be fulfilled and delivered to your location.
questions.check: What does the shipping section say about delivering to your country?
questions.say_example: This one says it may not ship to <the Philippines>. You could win it and never get it. I'd let it go.

questions.question: How many bids and watchers does the listing show?
questions.why: The screen shows 4 bids and 10 watchers, indicating high interest that might make winning difficult.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to strategically avoid highly competitive auctions to increase their chances of winning.
questions.check: How many bids and watchers does the listing show?
questions.say_example: <4> bids, <10> watchers on this one

questions.question: Does the estimated delivery window align with when you actually need the item?
questions.why: The listing displays an estimated delivery date range, and winning the auction means you must be willing to wait that long for the item to arrive.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to pass on an auction if the shipping timeline is too slow for their personal needs.
questions.check: What estimated delivery dates does the listing show?
questions.say_example: Delivery is <March 3 to 14>, and you said you need it by <the 1st>. Winning this one won't make it.

questions.question: Does the listing display a 'Reserve not met' notice, indicating that the seller has a hidden minimum price?
questions.why: In a reserve auction, simply being the highest bidder is not enough to win; your bid must exceed the hidden reserve price, which changes how you value and bid on the item.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to decide whether to avoid reserve auctions entirely or adjust their maximum bid to try and uncover the hidden threshold.
questions.check: Does the listing show 'Reserve not met'?
questions.say_example: This one has a hidden minimum price, and it hasn't been met. Even the top bid doesn't win until it clears that.

questions.question: Does the shipping section indicate the item is 'Local Pickup Only' rather than offering delivery?
questions.why: Bidding on a local pickup item by mistake means you will be contractually obligated to buy an item you cannot physically retrieve if you live far away.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the protection against accidentally committing to purchase an item that the seller refuses to ship.
questions.check: Does the shipping section say Local Pickup Only, and from where?
questions.say_example: This one is pickup only, from <Fort Frances>. Nobody ships it. Can you get there, or should I skip it?

questions.question: Does the listing display the visual 'Authenticity Guarantee' blue checkmark?
questions.why: For high-value items, this visual badge is the only guarantee that the item will be physically authenticated by eBay before delivery.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the security of knowing their expensive purchase is protected against counterfeits if the agent cannot verify the visual badge.
questions.check: Does the listing show the Authenticity Guarantee badge?
questions.say_example: No Authenticity Guarantee badge on this listing

questions.question: Is the photo labeled 'Stock photo' rather than the seller's own picture?
questions.why: Inspecting the item's photos allows you to verify its authenticity and avoid bidding on a counterfeit product.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to apply your personal expertise to spot subtle signs of a fake item before committing your money.
questions.check: Does the image carry a 'Stock photo' label?
questions.say_example: The picture is a stock photo. It's not the seller's own item, so you'd be bidding without seeing the real one.

questions.question: Do the details in the title match the item specifics table?
questions.why: The subtitle states the book is the 2009 sixth edition, but the item specifics list the publication year as 2008, creating uncertainty about the exact item being sold.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to notice the conflicting publication years and clarify which edition they are actually buying before committing to a bid.
questions.check: What does the title say, and what does the item specifics table say, for the same detail?
questions.say_example: The title says <2009, sixth edition>, but the specifics say <2008>. Those don't match, so it's not clear which one you'd get.

questions.question: Does the description add terms the top of the page doesn't show, like a payment deadline or a restocking fee?
questions.why: The description contains a red warning about a strict 24-hour payment deadline with a restocking fee, as well as a discrepancy in the hard drive size.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to catch punitive seller terms and item discrepancies before committing to a binding bid.
questions.check: What extra terms does the full description state that the listing panel doesn't?
questions.say_example: Down in the description it says pay within 24 hours or there's a restocking fee. The top of the page never mentions that.

questions.question: What feedback score and percentage does the seller show?
questions.why: Although the screen shows a 99.6% positive feedback score for the seller, checking the detailed reviews helps ensure there are no hidden red flags before committing your money.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to personally assess the seller's reliability and read specific buyer experiences before trusting them with your purchase.
questions.check: What feedback percentage and rating count does the seller info box show?
questions.say_example: Seller record - 99.6% positive, <2,341> ratings

questions.question: Does the seller's feedback score read zero?
questions.why: The screen shows the seller 'guanweidianzi' has a feedback score of 0, which could indicate a higher risk for a buyer.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to apply their own risk tolerance when evaluating an unestablished seller.
questions.check: What feedback score does the seller info box show?
questions.say_example: This seller has zero feedback. Nobody has bought from them before. Want me to find the same thing from a seller with a record?

questions.question: Is the same item listed at a fixed price, and for how much?
questions.why: The listing includes a link to see more of this specific HP laptop model, which could help ensure you are getting the best deal.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to compare alternatives and potentially find a better price or condition for the desired item.
questions.check: Does the page link a fixed-price listing of the same model, and at what price?
questions.say_example: The same laptop is Buy It Now for <$18.96>. If the bidding gets near that, the auction stops being a deal.

questions.question: Did your winning bid save you money compared to the fixed-price option you considered earlier?
questions.why: Comparing the final $14.60 bid to the initial $18.96 fixed-price listing confirms that participating in the auction was financially worthwhile.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the satisfaction of verifying that your bidding strategy successfully secured a better deal than the immediate purchase price.
questions.check: What was the final price, and what did the fixed-price twin cost?
questions.say_example: Won at <$14.60> - the Buy It Now twin was <$18.96>

questions.question: Is the shipping fee bigger than the current bid?
questions.why: The screen shows a shipping cost of US $163.22, which is nearly double the current US $91.00 bid for the used washing machine.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to reject an auction where the shipping fees make the total cost unreasonably high.
questions.check: What are the current bid and the shipping fee?
questions.say_example: The bid is <$91>, but shipping is <$163>. Shipping costs more than the machine. All in, it's <$254>.

questions.question: Are there mandatory import charges or customs duties listed below the standard shipping fee?
questions.why: For international listings, customs duties and import charges are often calculated and billed separately from the item price and standard shipping, significantly increasing the total cost.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to factor in steep, non-negotiable cross-border fees that might make a domestic listing a better deal.
questions.check: Does the listing show an import charges line, and for how much?
questions.say_example: There are import charges too, <$12.40> on top of shipping. That's part of what you'd pay.

questions.question: What do the current bid and shipping add up to?
questions.why: The bidding screen only shows the bid amount and omits the shipping fee from the listing screen, which hides the actual total cost of the transaction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to strictly control their total spending if the agent ignores shipping fees omitted from the active bidding screen.
questions.check: What current bid and shipping cost does the listing show?
questions.say_example: All in, this one is <$15.50> plus <$0.73> shipping right now, about <$16.23>.

children.label: Set the maximum bid
children.note: one of 4.1 to 4.3 sets the figure - or none: liZv types the bare starting bid. 4.4 then tunes the cents. the figure is fixed before the endgame and moves again only through 7.

questions.question: Is the current bid still within your budget?
questions.why: Evaluating the current bid of $42.00 ensures you do not waste time or money on an item that already exceeds your spending limit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the ability to personally weigh the current price against your own strict or flexible budget constraints.
questions.check: What is the current bid, against the budget you gave?
questions.say_example: The bid's at <$42> now. That's past the <$35> you gave me. Go higher, or let this one go?

children.label: Stage the bid
children.note: 5.1 opens the surface. accounts with no payment on file get 5.2 instead of a bid box - all three keepers who hit it end there. then 5.3 and 5.4; 5.5 and 5.6 on the review surface; 5.7 is one keeper's backup in case the page glitches. snipers stop here with the confirm staged and hand the last click to 6; immediate bidders pass straight through.

questions.question: Did a security challenge or CAPTCHA appear when you attempted to submit your bid amount?
questions.why: Automated agents or unusual browsing patterns can trigger anti-bot protections, which will completely block the bid submission until a human solves the challenge.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the auction because they are not alerted to step in and solve the security check before the clock runs out.
questions.check: Does the page show a CAPTCHA or verification challenge?
questions.say_example: eBay put up a human check before it takes the bid. I can't do that part. It's yours.

children.label: Provide a payment method
children.note: 5.2.1 as the prompts appear, then 5.2.2, with 5.2.3 stacked on top for dh72. 5.2.4 is the pass-through case - pre-wired accounts read their card inside the modal and never see the wall. no keeper who hits the wall gets past it.

questions.question: Does the page ask you to add or pick a payment method before bidding?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'Select payment method' modal that requires you to add a payment method before the system will process your auction bids.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to choose exactly which personal credit card or financial account is kept on file for automatic charges if you win.
questions.check: Does a modal ask for a payment method, and which saved methods does it list?
questions.say_example: eBay needs a card on file before it takes bids. You have a <Mastercard ending 4821>. Use that one?

questions.question: Does the page show an error that the item can't ship to your address?
questions.why: The screen displays an error stating the item cannot be shipped to your country, meaning this specific transaction cannot proceed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to provide an alternative shipping address or personally select which alternative seller to buy from.
questions.check: What does the red error text say about shipping to the selected address?
questions.say_example: eBay says this seller doesn't ship to <your country>, so the bid can't go through. Want me to find the same thing from one who does?

questions.question: Are you agreeing to have your payment method automatically charged if you win, or will you need to manually check out later?
questions.why: The confirmation screen often includes terms stating that the selected payment method will be automatically charged upon winning, changing when the money actually moves.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prepare for an immediate, automatic deduction from their account versus having a window of time to manually complete the payment.
questions.check: Does the confirmation say the payment method will be charged automatically if you win?
questions.say_example: Card gets charged automatically on a win - no separate checkout

questions.question: How much should you set as your maximum bid?
questions.why: The screen shows the 'Your max bid' field where entering an amount activates the 'Bid' button, establishing the absolute limit you are willing to pay.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to personally determine their true maximum willingness to pay based on their own valuation of the item.
questions.check: What current bid, shipping cost and suggested amounts does the bid form show?
questions.say_example: The bid's at <$15.50>, with <$0.73> shipping. What's the most you'll pay, all in? I'd make it an odd number like <$18.37>. Round numbers tie with other people's bids, and ties go to whoever bid first.

questions.question: Is the bid input field expecting the amount in the listing's native currency rather than your local converted currency?
questions.why: International listings display your local currency as an approximation, but the actual bid input field often requires the amount in the seller's native currency, making it easy to accidentally overbid by a huge margin if you enter the converted number.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to prevent a catastrophic overbid caused by entering a local currency value into a foreign currency input field.
questions.check: What currency symbol does the bid field carry?
questions.say_example: The bid box takes <pounds>. <£21.87> here is about <$27.50> of your money.

questions.question: Is the bid input field pre-filled with eBay's suggested minimum bid, requiring it to be cleared before typing your maximum?
questions.why: eBay often auto-populates the text box with the next minimum increment, which can lead to appended numbers (e.g., typing '50' into a box holding '15' makes '1550') or accidental minimum bids if not explicitly cleared.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user risks placing a drastically incorrect bid amount if the agent types into a field that already contains pre-filled numbers.
questions.check: Does the bid field show exactly the amount that was approved?
questions.say_example: The box came pre-filled, so it read <1550> instead of <50>. I cleared it and typed it fresh. It shows <50> now.

questions.question: What is the current status of this auction, and what is the minimum amount you need to bid?
questions.why: The screen shows a current bid of C $7.99 and explicitly states that you must enter C $8.49 or more to place a valid bid.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you lose the opportunity to personally evaluate the current price and minimum bid requirement against your own budget.
questions.check: What minimum bid does the page state?
questions.say_example: Minimum accepted bid <C $8.49>

questions.question: Is the entered amount at least the minimum the page requires?
questions.why: The screen displays helper text stating you must enter US $14.01 or more, and entering a lower amount triggers a red error message that blocks the bid.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent enters an invalid amount, the bid will be rejected and you risk losing the auction while precious seconds tick away.
questions.check: What minimum does the helper text state, and what is in the field?
questions.say_example: eBay wants <$14.01> or more, and your max is <$14>. It won't take the bid. Go to <$14.01>, or let this one go?

questions.question: Are my max bid amount, payment method, and shipping address correct before I proceed?
questions.why: Verifying the $40 max bid, the selected Mastercard, and the shipping address ensures you do not overpay or send the item to the wrong location.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to verify your exact maximum bid limit and ensure the correct payment method and shipping address are used if you win.
questions.check: What max bid, payment method and delivery address does the confirm screen show?
questions.say_example: Ready to bid. Max <$40>, your <Mastercard ending 4821>, shipping to <Home>. If you win, it's binding and the card is charged. Press to bid, or say change.

questions.question: Does the review screen mark duties or taxes as an estimate?
questions.why: The review screen explicitly marks the duties as an 'Estimate, final at checkout,' meaning the actual amount you are legally committing to pay if you win could be higher than the total currently shown.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to factor in the risk of fluctuating import fees and taxes before making a binding financial commitment.
questions.check: Does the duties line say 'Estimate, final at checkout'?
questions.say_example: The duties line says estimate, final at checkout. The real total can land higher than the <$54.20> showing now.

questions.question: Did the current bid change between the search results and the item details page?
questions.why: The search results showed the current bid as $0.25, but the item details page immediately displayed $0.55.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might fail to notice the sudden price jump and place a bid that no longer aligns with your expectations.
questions.check: Does the current bid on the listing match the price shown in the results?
questions.say_example: The results said <$0.25>, but the listing says <$0.55> now. Bids are landing while we look.

questions.question: Does the auction end time remain consistent across the different moments of the task?
questions.why: A consistent auction end time confirms that the same listing is being viewed and that the countdown timer is functioning correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The delegator loses the ability to verify that the agent is interacting with a single, stable auction listing throughout the task.
questions.check: Is the end time shown now the same as when the listing was first read?
questions.say_example: The end time changed since I first read it. That can mean a different listing, so I'm re-checking before anything else.

questions.question: Do you see the exact total cost of the bid and postage explicitly stated on the screen?
questions.why: Confirming only the explicitly stated amounts prevents errors from assuming or calculating an unshown total.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent hallucinates an unstated total cost, the user loses accurate visibility into the actual financial commitment.
questions.check: Does the page itself state a combined bid-plus-postage total?
questions.say_example: No combined total on screen - bid <£13.16> and postage <£3.35> shown separately

children.label: Time the confirm
children.note: immediate bidders run 6.6 the moment 5 is done (08WT, s_CE, B7Zu, fAtx). snipers set 6.1, arm 6.2 where the clock and the trigger need separate windows, then hold 6.3 while 6.4 and 6.5 loop until the chosen second arrives; then 6.6. fx1m runs the whole goal four listings at once; GYkw and liZv teach it and never fire.

questions.question: Should you place your bid now or wait until the auction is closer to ending?
questions.why: With 5 minutes and 53 seconds left on the auction, waiting to bid can prevent driving up the price prematurely.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to apply personal bidding strategies, like waiting until the last moment to avoid bidding wars.
questions.check: How much time does the countdown show?
questions.say_example: Everything's staged at <$40> max. Bid now, or hold it and press in the last <ten> seconds? Bidding early gives rivals time to push the price.

questions.question: Did the system reject your bid confirmation with an error stating you do not meet the seller's buyer requirements?
questions.why: Sellers can configure their listings to automatically block bids from users with unpaid item strikes or low feedback, stopping the transaction at the final step.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the immediate understanding that they are explicitly blocked by this seller and must abandon the listing to search for another.
questions.check: Does the page show an error that you don't meet the seller's buyer requirements?
questions.say_example: eBay refused the bid. It says this account doesn't meet the seller's buyer rules. That's the seller's setting, and I can't change it.

questions.question: What does the countdown show while the confirm is staged?
questions.why: The screen shows 46 seconds left, and waiting to confirm until the last moment prevents other bidders from having time to react.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the strategic advantage of bid sniping if the agent confirms the bid too early.
questions.check: What does the countdown on the confirmation screen show?
questions.say_example: I'm holding on the confirm screen. <46> seconds left. I'll press at <ten>.

questions.question: Is the countdown timer on the confirmation screen actively ticking down, or has it frozen?
questions.why: Network lag or a stale page state can cause the on-screen timer to freeze, meaning if you wait for it to reach the final seconds, the auction will actually end in the background before you click confirm.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to detect a stalled interface and switch to a backup tab or refresh before they miss the chance to submit their snipe bid.
questions.check: Has the countdown value changed between two reads?
questions.say_example: The countdown hasn't moved in a while. The page looks frozen, so I'm refreshing before it costs us the ending.

questions.question: Did the screen refresh to show your bid is no longer high enough to meet the new minimum?
questions.why: In the seconds between staging and confirming a bid, another buyer's proxy bid might have raised the current price past your staged maximum amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the chance to realize their staged bid is already dead and immediately enter a higher amount before the clock runs out.
questions.check: Does the page say the current bid is now at or above the staged maximum?
questions.say_example: Someone just pushed the price past your <$40>. The staged bid won't count now. Go higher, or let it go?

questions.question: Are the bid amounts and total number of bids consistent throughout the process?
questions.why: The screen shows the current bid logically increasing from $42.00 with 11 bids to a final winning bid of $46.00 with 16 bids.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to monitor the live competitiveness and logical progression of the auction.
questions.check: Do the bid count and price rise consistently across the screens?
questions.say_example: Bids climbed <$42> to <$46>, <11> to <16> bids - consistent

questions.question: Did the auction end with no bid recorded from this account?
questions.why: The screen showed the auction countdown reaching zero and ending before any bid amount was entered or the Place bid button was clicked.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to win the item because the agent failed to submit the bid before the auction ended.
questions.check: Does the page show the auction ended with no bid recorded from this account?
questions.say_example: The clock hit zero before the bid went in. It didn't count, and nothing was spent.

children.label: Recover from an outbid
children.note: entered from the red notice, at any distance from the close - seconds after 6.6 (s_CE, 08WT) or inside a live hold (B7Zu, T5mb). 7.1 then 7.2, looping until the lead holds or the clock kills it - 08WT cycles three times, T5mb runs it inside the final 25 seconds and still loses. 7.3 closes each cycle.

questions.question: Is the bid amount you entered valid and ready to submit?
questions.why: A red exclamation mark in the input field indicates that the entered value of '208.1' has an invalid format or increment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to correct a formatting error before submission, which could cause your bid to be rejected by the system.
questions.check: Does the bid field show an error mark against the entered value?
questions.say_example: The box flagged <208.1> as invalid, so I retyped it as <208.10>. No error now.

questions.question: Does the page say another bidder's maximum is above yours?
questions.why: The screen shows a warning that another bidder's maximum bid exceeded yours, requiring a decision on whether to submit a higher amount.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally evaluate your budget limit in real-time when deciding if the item is still worth the higher price.
questions.check: Does the page show an outbid notice?
questions.say_example: You've been outbid already. Someone's max was over your <$40>. Go higher, or stop here?

questions.question: Did your bid put you in the lead, and what's the current price?
questions.why: Verifying the confirmation message and current bid amount ensures your maximum bid was accepted and you are currently winning the auction.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the immediate reassurance of seeing your winning status and knowing exactly how much of your maximum bid is currently being used.
questions.check: Does the page say you're the highest bidder, and at what current bid?
questions.say_example: Your bid's in. You're the high bidder at <$46>, and your max is <$51>.

children.label: Verify the outcome
children.note: 8.1 while seconds remain, 8.2 at zero - the won state often needs a reload to appear. 8.3 whenever the auction resolves; 8.4 is one keeper's full audit. a loss ends the task here (T5mb, dh72, GYkw).

questions.question: Does the maximum recorded on the page match the amount that was approved?
questions.why: If an agent or user inputs an extra digit, the resulting proxy bid could be financially ruinous, and eBay only allows retractions for obvious typos if done quickly before the auction ends.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the critical, time-sensitive opportunity to use the platform's emergency reversal process to cancel a disastrously high bid.
questions.check: Does the max bid recorded on the page match the amount that was approved?
questions.say_example: The page shows your max as <$1,000>, but you approved <$10>. That's wrong, so I'm starting a retraction now, while the rules still allow it.

questions.question: Does the status explicitly say 'Reserve not met' next to your winning bid amount?
questions.why: Even if you are the highest bidder, a small visual indicator stating 'Reserve not met' means you will not actually win the item when the auction ends unless you bid higher.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user falsely believes they have secured the item because they are the highest bidder, completely missing that the hidden reserve price blocks the sale.
questions.check: Does the status line show 'Reserve not met' beside your bid?
questions.say_example: You're the top bid, but it says reserve not met. At this price, you still don't win it.

questions.question: Did you actually confirm the bid, or is the item already sold?
questions.why: The screen shows a 'SOLD' badge and a final price, contradicting the narrator's claim that a bid was confirmed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user would falsely believe they have an active bid on the item when it has actually already been sold to someone else.
questions.check: Does the page show a SOLD or ended state with no bid from this account?
questions.say_example: This auction already ended. It sold for <$14.60>, and no bid of ours is on it. Nothing was spent.

questions.question: Do you see the exact phrase 'You won this auction' on the screen?
questions.why: Assuming the auction is won when the screen only confirms you are the highest bidder misrepresents the actual outcome shown.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate tracking of their auction if the agent falsely reports a final win instead of a pending highest-bidder status.
questions.check: Does the page literally say you won, not just that you're the highest bidder?
questions.say_example: The page only says highest bidder. It doesn't say you won, so I'm not calling it won yet.

questions.question: Does the page say you won, and what is the final price?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Congratulations! You won this item' banner along with the final price of US $0.31.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses confirmation of their auction victory and the knowledge of the final purchase price.
questions.check: What does the ended-auction banner say, and at what final price?
questions.say_example: It's over, and you won. <$0.31>, plus <$5.50> shipping.

questions.question: Does the final bid price logically follow from your maximum bid and the previous current bid?
questions.why: The final price of $0.31 is consistent with a maximum bid of $0.66 and a previous high bid of $0.30, confirming the automatic bidding system worked correctly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify that the platform's automatic bidding system executed their bid correctly without overcharging.
questions.check: Is the final price at or below the approved maximum?
questions.say_example: Something's off. The final price is <$48>, but your max was <$46>. I'm opening the bid history to see what happened.

questions.question: Which auctions did you win, and did your sniping strategy keep the prices under your target?
questions.why: Checking the four windows confirms that you won three auctions near your $120 goal while safely losing the one that exceeded it.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the satisfaction of seeing your multi-window sniping strategy succeed and knowing exactly which items you secured within your budget.
questions.check: Which of the watched auctions show a won banner, and at what final prices?
questions.say_example: Won <3> of <4> - <$118>, <$112>, <$119.50>; lost the one that passed <$120>

questions.question: Does the final total cost, including shipping, align with your initial budget?
questions.why: The screen shows a $9.99 winning bid and $8.99 shipping, which totals $18.98 and successfully stays under the $20 budget.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the financial reassurance of manually calculating that the final combined costs respect their maximum budget.
questions.check: What do the winning bid and shipping add up to, against the budget you gave?
questions.say_example: The bid and shipping come to <$18.98>. That's over the <$15> you gave me. You should know before paying.

questions.question: How close to the end of the auction did you place your winning bid?
questions.why: Comparing the recorded bid time of 10:12:17 to the auction end time of 10:12:20 confirms exactly how narrow your margin of victory was.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the strategic insight and personal satisfaction of knowing exactly how close to the final deadline their successful bid was recorded.
questions.check: What bid time and end time does the bid history show?
questions.say_example: Winning bid landed at <10:12:17>, three seconds before the close

children.label: Close out the win
children.note: 9.1 on every win. 9.2 and 9.3 where the buyer bothers; 9.4 loops back to 2 when the session hunts more - Zkom six times, fx1m until a three-win quota releases the fourth. no keeper in the corpus completes a payment.

questions.question: Is the checkout total shown, with shipping, the amount you want to pay?
questions.why: The checkout screen displays a total of $347.64 for the three items, which represents your final financial commitment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to personally verify that the final combined cost aligns with their budget before the order is confirmed.
questions.check: What order total does the checkout page show?
questions.say_example: Checkout says <$347.64> for <the three drives> together. Only you can pay. Press to pay, or say stop.

questions.question: Do you actually see a checkout page displaying the total order amount, or just multiple item pages?
questions.why: This matters because the screen at 1:39 only shows four panes of eBay item pages, contradicting the claim that a checkout page with a $347.64 total is visible.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses accurate verification of their final costs if the agent hallucinates a checkout page and order total that do not actually exist on the screen.
questions.check: Does the page show a checkout order total?
questions.say_example: I don't see a checkout total on this page yet, so I'm not quoting one.

questions.question: Are the current search results showing the most up-to-date auctions ending soonest?
questions.why: Refreshing the search results for 'pcs' ensures you are looking at the most current listings and accurate time remaining, as auction statuses change rapidly.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to guarantee the agent is acting on real-time auction data rather than stale search results.
questions.check: What time-left values do the refreshed results show?
questions.say_example: Refreshed the results before the next auction - countdowns current

questions.question: Should you confirm this bid for a fourth item, or cancel it since you have already won three?
questions.why: The confirmation popup shows your $120.55 max bid, providing a final opportunity to click the 'X' and cancel if you have already acquired enough of these items.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent might automatically confirm the bid without realizing you already won enough of this item, resulting in unnecessary spending.
questions.check: How many wins does the page show against the number you asked for, with another bid staged?
questions.say_example: You've already won <three>, and that's what you asked for. A fourth bid is still staged. I'm closing it, unless you say bid.
